title: Enable format ruff on tests
body:
This removes `# fmt: off` from all files in tests and runs `ruff format` on them.

A few places required e.g. manual rewrapping in order to come out non-horribly (and pass line length check etc.).  I scrolled briefly through every change to check that nothing is totally crazy.

Changes are applied independently in a series of commits, so if any of this should *not* be done, it can be at least partially isolated.

If we think this changeset is too large in volume, it would be possible to merge e.g. the first few commits.

A few tests in fio/ historically had meaningful trailing whitespace (to check parser robustness), but I didn't find any such tests although I paid special attention to parser tests.  I think we have already removed them in order for the tests to pass `ruff check`, typically by adding `\n\` (manual newline followed by "please do not make a newline now") to long triplequoted strings so they end with whitespace without offending the ruff linter.

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [ ] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)
- [ ] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://ase-lib.org/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [ ] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://ase-lib.org/development/tests.html)
- [ ] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [ ] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: askhl

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Looking at test_harmonic.py: I think the comment alignment is an acceptable sacrifice on the altar of consistency. The reference data could maybe be stuffed into a .json file?

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment suggests moving reference data into a .json file, which is a concrete code change suggestion, even though it is phrased tentatively ('could maybe').

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
@ajjackson @yuzie007 This ruffs the whole test suite, for better or worse.  This can also be done in smaller chunks than this MR, e.g., by creating a new MR that includes only some of the first commits.

But probably we won't get too much trouble with merge conflicts due to ruffing of tests.  The actual code is more liable to cause merge conflicts if we ruff it in large chunks.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I merged from master preferring changes from master where there were conflicts, then re-ruffed as necessary.

I will merge soon unless someone thinks it'll cause too many conflicts.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @askhl for the Ruff work! I think we can go ahead. Skimming over the changes, only in a few places (below), I feel that the readability might be substantially degraded, but we can later address them in separate MRs.

- `ase/test/calcuator/test_harmonic.py`
- `ase/test/cell/test_niggli.py`
- `ase/test/constraints/test_parameteric_constr.py`

thread.actionability_reasoning: This is a general approval comment with meta-discussion about the PR. While it mentions specific files with readability concerns, it explicitly defers any action to separate future MRs and does not request any concrete change in this PR.
